chapter: Raymond Scott, Kirby and postwar bands
title: Getting Chubby Jackson and Ralph Burns hired
summary: Hinton sorts out dates; Leeman says he got Chubby Jackson into Barnet's band in 1940 and recommended Ralph Burns to Woody Herman.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Most of the jazz magazines, and most of the histories of you says '47 with Glen Gray. Now when were you with -- and you say I'm going back, I would like to keep this in perspective, if I possibly can, according to what you want -- it's your story. But when were you with Woodie and when did you recommend Ralph Burns.
Well, I got Chubby Jackson his job in Barnet's band recently -- I always needed a bass player.
That was back in '40. I was instrumental in getting Chubby ...
But in '43 you were with Woody.
This was before you went home for business. Is that right?

Okay. Because we missed that -- so between 1940 and 1943, you were with Woody, and this was when you got Chubby in the band because you needed a good bass player, and certainly he was one, and you got Ralph Burns -- you recommended Ralph Burns.
Well, tell us about that because Ralph Burns is probably one of the most formidable arrangers in the world.
